originality.rationale: The identical random IFS and Lebesgue stationarity are already in Homburg–Kalle and are credited; a different Pelikan process has known low-lag correlations. Inspected primary full texts and targeted searches did not identify the exact time covariance for the uniform inverse-branch stationary process, its p↔1-p duality, the cusp, or the parity Gaussian window; priority uncertainty for equivalent uncatalogued random-walk treatments remains. A previously obtained heterochaos baker-map half-line calculation contains equivalent equal-probability parity constants; that critical mechanism alone is not claimed as new. The complete random one-dimensional model, all-p covariance identity, duality, cusp and Gaussian parameter crossover are not implied by that prior specialized calculation.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued exact solution for the weighted half-line shift resolvent could subsume the covariance if it includes this coordinate observable.
Publication-priority searches do not prove absolute novelty; an independent subject-expert assessment is absent.

value.rationale: The exact stationary time-observable response remains invariant under Lyapunov-sign reversal yet has a sharp nonanalytic integrated-correlation maximum at its intermittency boundary. The explicit all-lag, parity-dependent n^{-3/2} and Gaussian critical-window laws quantitatively resolve a naturally motivated question throughout an infinite matched-base family, not an arbitrary finite sample.
